entries.title: Matthew 27:1
segments: And when the morning came, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus, how they might put him to death.

entries.title: Matthew 27:2
segments: After they had bound him, they led him away, and handed him over to Pilate, the Roman Governor.

entries.title: Matthew 27:3
segments: Then when Judas, his betrayer, saw that he was condemned, he repented and brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders.

entries.title: Matthew 27:4
segments: "I have sinned," he said, "in betraying innocent blood!" "What is that to us?" they answered; "you must see to that."

entries.title: Matthew 27:5
segments: And flinging down the silver into the Sanctuary, he rushed out, and went and hanged himself.

entries.title: Matthew 27:6
segments: The chief priests took the money, and said, "It would be wrong to put it into the temple-treasury, because it is the price of blood."

entries.title: Matthew 27:7
segments: So after the consultation they bought the Potter's Field with it, for a burial-place for strangers.

entries.title: Matthew 27:8
segments: That is the reason why, to this day, the field is called "The Field of Blood."

entries.title: Matthew 27:9
segments: Then was fulfilled the word spoken by the prophet Jeremiah: And I took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him who had been priced, whom certain of the Children of Israel had priced;

entries.title: Matthew 27:10
segments: and gave them for the Potter's Field, as the Lord had appointed me.

entries.title: Matthew 27:11
segments: Now Jesus stood before the Governor, and the Governor questioned him. "Are you the King of the Jews?" he asked.

entries.title: Matthew 27:12
segments: "it is as you say," answered Jesus; but while he was being accused by the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing.

entries.title: Matthew 27:13
segments: Then Pilate said to him, "Do you not hear what they are testifying against you?"

entries.title: Matthew 27:14
segments: But he made no answer, not even to one charge; insomuch that the Governor was greatly astonished.

entries.title: Matthew 27:15
segments: Now it was the Governor's custom, during the Passover, to release to the people any one prisoner whom they selected.

entries.title: Matthew 27:16
segments: At that time they had a notorious prisoner named Barabbas.

entries.title: Matthew 27:17
segments: So when they had assembled, Pilate said to them, "Whom do you want me to release to you, Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?"

entries.title: Matthew 27:18
segments: He knew well that it was because of enmity that they had brought Jesus before him.

entries.title: Matthew 27:19
segments: And while he was seated upon the judgment-seat, his wife had sent to him, saying, "Have nothing to do with that innocent man, for I have suffered many things today, in a dream, because of him."

entries.title: Matthew 27:20
segments: But the chief priests and the elders urged the crowds to ask for Barabbas, and to destroy Jesus.

entries.title: Matthew 27:21
segments: So when Pilate said to them, "Which of the two do you want me to release unto you?" they said, "Barabbas."

entries.title: Matthew 27:22
segments: And Pilate asked, "What then shall I do with Jesus, who is called Christ?" What one voice they shouted, "Let him be crucified!"

entries.title: Matthew 27:23
segments: But Pilate said, "Why, what evil has he done?" But they kept shouting the more fiercely, "Let him be crucified!"

entries.title: Matthew 27:24
segments: So when Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but that on the contrary a riot was threatening, he took water and washed his hands in the presence of the crowd, saying: "I am innocent of the blood of this man; you must answer for it."

entries.title: Matthew 27:25
segments: All the people answered, "His blood be upon us and upon our children."

entries.title: Matthew 27:26
segments: Then he released Barabbas to them, but Jesus he scourged, and delivered to be crucified.

entries.title: Matthew 27:27
segments: Then the soldiers of the Governor took Jesus into the Praetorium, and gathered all the battalion together.

entries.title: Matthew 27:28
segments: They stripped him and put on him a scarlet robe.

entries.title: Matthew 27:29
segments: And they twisted a thorny crown for him, and put it on his head, and placed a reed in his right hand. Then they knelt before him, in mockery, crying, "Hail, King of the Jews!"

entries.title: Matthew 27:30
segments: And they spit upon him, and took the reed and struck him on the head, again and again.

entries.title: Matthew 27:31
segments: At last, when they had finished their mocking, they took the robe off, and put his own garments on him, and led him away to crucify him.

entries.title: Matthew 27:32
segments: And as they went out they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name, whom they compelled to go with them to carry his cross.

entries.title: Matthew 27:33
segments: And when they came to a place called Golgotha (the word means "Place of a Skull"),

entries.title: Matthew 27:34
segments: they gave Jesus wine to drink, mingled with gall. But after tasting it he refused to drink it.

entries.title: Matthew 27:35
segments: After crucifying him, they parted his garments among them by casting lots.

entries.title: Matthew 27:36
segments: Then they sat and watched him there.

entries.title: Matthew 27:37
segments: They also placed above his head his accusation written, This is Jesus The King of the Jews

entries.title: Matthew 27:38
segments: At that time two robbers, also, were crucified with him; one on his right hand, the other on his left.

entries.title: Matthew 27:39
segments: Those who passed by, reviled him, wagging their heads saying:

entries.title: Matthew 27:40
segments: "You who were going to destroy the Temple and build it in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross!"

entries.title: Matthew 27:41
segments: In like manner the chief priests, too, with the Scribes and elders, kept taunting him:

entries.title: Matthew 27:42
segments: "He saved others," they said, "himself he cannot save. He, the King of Israel! Let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe on him!

entries.title: Matthew 27:43
segments: He put his trust in God: let Him deliver him now, if He cares for him. For he said, `I am the Son of God!'"

entries.title: Matthew 27:44
segments: In the same way the robbers also who were being crucified with him, dept reviling him.

entries.title: Matthew 27:45
segments: Now from noon darkness fell upon the whole land, until three o'clock in the afternoon.

entries.title: Matthew 27:46
segments: But at three o'clock Jesus cried out in loud voice, "Eli, Eli, Lama Sabachthani?" (That is to say, "My God, my God, why hast You forsaken me?")

entries.title: Matthew 27:47
segments: When they heard this, some of the bystanders said "He is calling for Elijah!"

entries.title: Matthew 27:48
segments: At once, one of them ran, and took a sponge, and filling it with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave him to drink.

entries.title: Matthew 27:49
segments: But the rest said: "Let be! Let us see whether Elijah is coming to save him!"

entries.title: Matthew 27:50
segments: And Jesus cried again with a loud voice, and yielded up his spirit.

entries.title: Matthew 27:51
segments: And lo, the veil of the sanctuary was torn in two, from the top to the bottom;

entries.title: Matthew 27:52
segments: the earth quaked; the rocks split; the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised.

entries.title: Matthew 27:53
segments: And coming forth out of the tombs, after his resurrection, they went into the holy city and appeared to many.

entries.title: Matthew 27:54
segments: When the Roman captain and the soldiers who were with him, guarding Jesus, saw the earthquake and all that happened, they were greatly terrified and said, "Certainly this man must have been God's Son."

entries.title: Matthew 27:55
segments: And there were present several women who were looking on from a distance; they had followed Jesus from a Galilee, ministering to him:

entries.title: Matthew 27:56
segments: among them being Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee's sons.

entries.title: Matthew 27:57
segments: When it was eventide, there came a rich man of Arimathea, named Joseph, who was himself a disciple of Jesus.

entries.title: Matthew 27:58
segments: This man went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.

entries.title: Matthew 27:59
segments: Pilate then commanded that it be given over to him.

entries.title: Matthew 27:60
segments: So Joseph took the body, and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth, and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had cut in the rock; and after rolling a great stone against the opening of the tomb, he went away.

entries.title: Matthew 27:61
segments: And Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary, sitting opposite the tomb.

entries.title: Matthew 27:62
segments: The day after--that is, the day following the Preparation--the chief priests and Pharisees went in a body to Pilate and said:

entries.title: Matthew 27:63
segments: "We recollect, Sir, that when he was living this imposter said, `I will rise again after three days.'

entries.title: Matthew 27:64
segments: Now therefore give orders to have the sepulcher securely guarded until the third day, for fear his disciples may come and steal him away, and then tell the people, `He is risen from the dead'; and so the last error will be worse than the first."

entries.title: Matthew 27:65
segments: "You can have a guard," said Pilate. "Go your way, make it as secure as you can."

entries.title: Matthew 27:66
segments: So they went and made the sepulcher secure, by sealing the stone in the presence of the guard.
